title: Sanctification is free gift, not earned by prior acts
source_text: XIX. Nec tamen gratia illa per quam intus sancti justique in conspectu Dei reddimur, tribuenda est actuum illorum, qui etiam ex divina ordinatione praecedunt, merito & efficaciae. Etenim sanctificatio & adoptio fidelium Dei donum est plane gratuitum, nec eam aut poenitentia, aut fides praerequisita per se efficere aut promereri potest. Ideoque ab Apostolo simpliciter δωρεὰν, donum Dei gratuitum vocatur Rom. 6. vers. ult. Stipendia peccati mors; donum autem Dei vita aeterna. Quippe, juxta sententiam doctissimorum interpretum, Diodati scilicet & Bezae, vita aeterna ibi rationem non habet subjecti, sed praedicati. Nec simpliciter intendit Apostolus dicere vitam aeter-nam esse quid quod gratis a Deo donatur, sed potius justitiam τὴν δικαιοσύνην, quam Deus gratuito nobis donat, dum nos Spiritu & Verbo regenerat, nos ad vitam aeter-nam, tanquam ejus finem & praemium ducere; sicut peccatum impoenitentibus, & pec-cati servis mortem aeternam affert.
pass_a_gloss: Yet that grace by which we are inwardly made holy and just in God's sight is not to be ascribed to the merit and efficacy of those acts which, even by divine ordinance, precede. For the sanctification and adoption of believers is plainly God's free gift, and neither repentance nor the faith prerequisite can of itself effect or merit it. Therefore by the Apostle it is simply called God's free gift (Romans 6, last verse): The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life. For, according to the judgment of the most learned interpreters, namely Diodati and Beza, eternal life there has the role not of subject but of predicate. Nor does the Apostle simply intend to say that eternal life is something freely given by God, but rather that the righteousness which God freely gives us when he regenerates us by Spirit and Word leads us to eternal life as its end and reward; just as sin brings eternal death upon the impenitent and slaves of sin.
pass_b_english: Prior acts do not merit or efficiently cause sanctification; it is God's free gift.
Rom 6:23 with Diodati/Beza: eternal life as predicate of the free gift of justifying/regenerating grace.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1053.
